Replay

Framework completion plan

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Completion gatesOrder of workDeferred game workWorking record

Priority set on 2026-09-20: finish Replay as a usable multiplayer framework. The scope was explicitly redirected away from achieving 100% parity across every ported game. This plan supersedes exhaustive game-parity requirements in the original roadmap and individual port ledgers. Those ledgers remain useful history and follow-up backlogs; their open rows do not automatically block the framework.

Keep Kit, original games and separate Replay versions independently runnable. Preserving them is still required. Deferred parity is not a claim of equivalence.

Status: the framework-first implementation, representative validation and experimental delivery assessment are complete. See the final requirement audit. Broader historical parity and unverified platform/deployment work remain explicitly listed as follow-up.

Completion gates#

Area Required framework result Representative evidence
Simulation core Restore/replay includes entity lifetime, RNG, commands and events; invalid operations are transactional and bounded Existing core/recording tests and Hello
Authoring and Godot Documented offline-to-network workflow, input capture, reusable scene binding and event reconciliation, useful diagnostics Hello plus one cross-entity gameplay change
Networking policies Explicit working contracts for server authority, cooperative/owner-driven interactions, competitive prediction and deterministic P2P One representative scenario for each policy, reusing existing ports
Identity and setup Reusable create/join/rejoin; authenticated transport binding; bounded errors and credential persistence Party/Room and P2P party integration; native two-player and browser recovery now have focused acceptance
Recovery Planned/crash migration, reconnect, late join, returned host, save/restore and content fencing preserve their documented guarantees Existing recovery fixtures; fix shared defects they reveal
Transport support Supported native/browser combinations work through the common API; deployment requirements and unverified integrations are explicit Focused ENet/RTC/transport tests; live Steam/platform checks tracked separately until available
Stabilization Resolve shared correctness failures, bound resource use, and measure representative CPU/memory/bandwidth and rollback/recovery cost Existing comparisons plus focused reruns for changed framework paths
Delivery Coherent public API, runnable minimal examples, setup/recovery documentation, compatibility policy and an evidence-backed experimental release assessment A concise acceptance audit against these gates

The final assessment maps each criterion to its evidence and limitations. Audit that evidence before expanding support claims. A technical gate can close without every game being a finished remake. The framework still needs credible authoring/behavior validation; game-specific visual fidelity is separate.

Order of work#

  1. Native two-player authenticated P2P integration now passes creator/guest return, endpoint replacement and a browser regression. Its bounded support and remaining deployment restrictions are recorded in the current gap list.
  2. The shared framework audit now maps these gates and current checks. Its remaining concrete tasks are tracked in the gap list; existing recovery/networking evidence is reused where its scope fits.
  3. Close that list, including shared event-loss/recovery issues when reproduced. Use games to expose library problems; move game-only differences to follow-up.
  4. Consolidate public setup APIs, examples and documentation. Complete one representative authoring comparison and the supported-configuration assessment.

Deferred game work#

Full Scrapyard content completion, every original gauntlet, exact particles/audio, matching every menu and game-specific behavior, and repeated full-game parity campaigns are follow-up work unless they expose a missing framework primitive or shared correctness defect. Existing ports remain available as testbeds.

Do not expand a port solely to mark its ledger complete. Do not rerun all games after an isolated change. Run the affected framework checks and representative integration cases, then continue to the next framework gap.

Working record#

Keep this plan and a short current gap list authoritative. Preserve prior results, but avoid repeatedly reading or duplicating the complete history. New evidence should contain the changed sources/identifiers, relevant logs and reproduction commands; large repeated source snapshots and unrelated game matrices are unnecessary.
